conventions.convention: For a finitely generated field extension K/k, a separating transcendence basis is a finite transcendence basis t such that K/k(t) is finite separable; the empty tuple is allowed.

A standard smooth presentation has n ≥ c ≥ 0, an invertible c-by-c Jacobian minor, and relative dimension n−c; the minor may be placed in the first c columns and principal localization may be absorbed into the presentation.

Proj uses homogeneous primes avoiding the irrelevant ideal, with standard charts Spec((S_xi)_0); arbitrary homogeneous ideals, including nonradical ideals, are allowed, and S_+=S gives the empty scheme.
The binary resultant uses the nominated degrees even if a leading coefficient vanishes, descending monomial bases, and the F block before the G block.
For a zero-dimensional projective k-scheme, total length is the sum of local-ring lengths multiplied by residue-field degrees over k; the empty sum is 0.
The universal differentials construction imposes additivity, Leibniz, and vanishing on the base; it assumes no finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If R→S is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime, and S' is the integral closure of the image of R in S, then there are a finite R-subalgebra T⊆S' and finitely many g_i∈T such that Spec(S) is homeomorphic to U=⋃D_T(g_i) in Spec(T), and T_{g_i}≅S_{g_i}; for every g∈T with D_T(g)⊆U, T_g≅S_g.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, R=k[x0,x1,x2], and F,G be nonzero positive-degree homogeneous forms of degrees d,e with no common nonconstant factor. For X=Proj(R/(F,G)), X is nonempty and finite and its total length over k is de.
For a field k and a finite-type integral domain A over k, the integral closure of A in Frac(A) is a finite A-module.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-presentation map R→S and q∈Spec(S), with p=q∩R, the map is standard smooth at q iff R_p→S_q is flat and S⊗_R κ(p) is geometrically regular at q.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A standard smooth R-algebra S is finitely presented and flat over R, with no hypothesis on R; R may be non-Noetherian or have zero divisors.
For any field k, algebraic closure K of k, and homogeneous forms F,G of nominated positive degrees d,e, including zero forms, Res_d,e(F,G)=0 iff F and G vanish together at some point of P¹(K).
Assume the Axiom of Choice. If R→S is finite type, S' is the integral closure of the image of R in S, and q is a prime where R→S is quasi-finite, then some g∈S' outside q gives S'_g≅S_g.

concerns.concern: Convention 4 states κ(p)=S_p/pS_p for a homogeneous projective point p. This is false in general: for Proj k[x0,x1], the generic point p=(0) would have the stated field k(x0,x1), while its actual Proj residue field is k(x1/x0). The Proj residue field is computed from the degree-zero chart local ring. This conflicts with downstream residue-degree uses in the projective total-length chain.

Proof step 1.5 asserts that mT⊆q'T for every maximal ideal n of S, hence R→N_i is local. Take R=k[t]_(t), S=R[x] (standard smooth with c=0,g=1), and n=(tx−1). Then S/n≅k(t), so n is maximal and n∩R=(0); t∈m becomes a unit in S_n. The asserted inclusion and locality fail, so step 4.1 cannot apply the local flatness lemma for this n. The flatness claim is true, but the proof needs localization at the contraction or an equivalent repair; this lemma feeds thm-ag-standard-smooth-geometric-regularity.

Proof step 1.3 factors F=u∏p_i^a_i and concludes F|H after establishing only p_i|H for each i. That establishes the factors only to the first power; the proof must iterate the primality argument to obtain the multiplicities. The lemma is true, but this step does not prove the claim as written and feeds the complete-intersection Hilbert-series and projective-length chain.
